note: Ten real excerpts from the learner's Software Systems notes, used read-only. Only paths, line ranges and SHA-256 of the excerpt text are stored; the benchmark reads the text from the vault and refuses to run if a hash differs. Objectives and expected routes were written before any model was run. Expected routes are for the algorithm module (numeric arrays: index, bubble sort, linear and binary search).

excerpts.objective: Memory as an array of bytes: a byte is read or written by giving its address, like reading an array element by its position

expected.reason: algorithm (index): reading one element by its zero-based position is what the module traces; virtual-to-physical mapping is not shown

excerpts.objective: argv holds the program path in argv[0] and the user's arguments in argv[1] to argv[argc-1]

expected.reason: elements are strings (character pointers); the module's arrays are integers only

excerpts.objective: A pipe is a fixed-size circular buffer: the read and write indices wrap around, and the writer or reader blocks when it is full or empty

expected.reason: needs a circular buffer with two wrapping indices and blocking; no module has it

excerpts.objective: sort orders lines alphabetically, character by character, so 5 comes after 30; sort -r reverses that order

expected.reason: needs lexicographic string comparison; the module's bubble sort orders numbers ascending, which would teach the wrong order

excerpts.objective: Two threads touching disjoint odd and even indices of a shared array need no synchronisation

expected.reason: needs two concurrent threads over disjoint index sets; a single-threaded trace cannot show it

excerpts.objective: The check, read and increment of index_counter must be one critical section, or two threads can take indexes 999 and 1000

expected.reason: needs interleaved threads on a check-then-act sequence

excerpts.objective: A race condition: unsynchronised threads updating a shared counter give a result that depends on their timing

expected.reason: needs a thread-interleaving trace of a shared counter

excerpts.objective: A test-and-set spinlock built from a separate read and write fails when the scheduler interrupts between them

expected.reason: needs a scheduler interleaving trace with an atomic instruction

excerpts.objective: A process moves between the running, ready and blocked states

expected.reason: a stable state diagram: the tutor draws it in the reply; no module needed

excerpts.objective: A file descriptor is an index into the process's descriptor table, whose entries point into the system-wide open file table

expected.reason: needs a two-level table of references with offsets and reference counts
